A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Cond-FiP despite the changed title and organization. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original benchmark results, encoder/decoder ablations, distribution-shift experiments, and Sachs data analysis in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds complex-noise experiments in Appendix H and counterfactual-generation results in Appendix K.2.

M1.justification: The alternating-attention encoder, conditional codebooks, adaptive normalization, training losses, and fixed-point generation procedure are retained. The counterfactual evaluation tests the existing model without introducing a revised architecture or algorithm.

E1.justification: V3 adds counterfactual generation across the LIN/RFF, IN/OUT, and 10–100-node settings. Appendix H also adds 12 multimodal-noise scenarios using Large Backdoor and Weak Arrow from CSuite. These extend both causal task requirements and input-noise coverage; the earlier synthetic and Sachs evaluations remain.

E2.justification: DoWhy, DECI, and FiP remain the primary comparators, and the separate CausalNF comparison is retained. DoWhy remains absent from the 50-sample experiments. The added evaluations use the existing primary comparator set.

E3.justification: The principal splits, metrics, and graph sizes remain unchanged. Added experiments specify six Gaussian-mixture configurations and counterfactual testing with inferred noise and true graphs. Batch documentation changes from size 2 in v2 to effective size 8 with gradient accumulation in v3; this does not establish whether training changed or accumulation was previously undisclosed.

E4.justification: Appendix H adds a robustness test using six multimodal-noise variants on two CSuite datasets. Existing encoder/decoder ablations, shift-strength tests, scarce-data experiments, inferred-graph evaluations, and large-context analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V3 newly describes plot summaries as means and standard errors. For example, Figure 6 adds this description to the retained CSuite plot, whereas v2 Figure 2 only specified RMSE across nine datasets. Tabular mean/standard-error reporting remains unchanged, and additional training runs or seeds are not established.

E6.justification: V3 adds complex-noise results and substantially weaker counterfactual performance: Table 30 reports Cond-FiP versus FiP RMSE of 0.56 versus 0.19 for RFF OUT at 100 nodes. Two retained Cond-FiP entries also change at 100 nodes/RFF OUT: interventional generation changes from 0.58 to 0.56 in Table 3, and 50-sample generation from 0.68 to 0.65 in v2 Table 12/v3 Table 14. Most other tabulated values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a brief Jacobian-based justification for ANM invertibility using triangular structure and nonzero diagonal elements. The existing SCM assumptions, DAG-attention mathematics, inverse-generator derivation, and finite-step fixed-point reasoning are retained.

C1.justification: The central contribution of amortized SCM inference without parameter updates is retained. V3's conclusion explicitly includes complex-noise generalization and acknowledges poor counterfactual generation, modestly extending and qualifying the stated capabilities. The title and terminology changes do not themselves change the contribution.

C2.justification: V3 adds an explanation of counterfactual failure involving inferred noise, explains why hard-intervention support prevents evaluation of Sachs soft interventions, and clarifies that distribution shift concerns Cond-FiP while baselines train on each test distribution. It also narrows the encoder-ablation interpretation from linear/nonlinear-only robustness to nonlinear-only robustness. These substantially refine applicability and interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds detailed SCM sampling counts, gradient accumulation, memory estimates, and computational-cost discussion. It also adds an anonymized code link, implementation locations, and non-executable/future-release caveats while retaining the public GitHub availability statement. These access descriptions are not fully consistent.

R1.justification: V3 broadens the background on meta-learning, in-context learning, amortized sampling, and causal inference, adding works including Finn et al. (2017), Garnelo et al. (2018), Dhir et al. (2024), and Sauter et al. (2025). Several older background citations disappear, but the central positioning as an amortized extension of FiP remains.

P1.justification: V3 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, method exposition, and experimental narrative. It adds an amortized-inference overview, moves Related Works after Experiments, relocates DAG-attention and training details to appendices, and reorganizes the appendices around experiments and limitations.

P2.justification: Tables 1–3 move from the main text to Appendix C, while multiple summary plots become prominent. The scarce-data display expands from one interventional setting to three tasks using largely existing appendix results. Figure 7 and Table 30 display new experiments, and numerous captions and table placements change.

improvement.justification: V3 provides a clearer and more candid account of Cond-FiP's capabilities through complex-noise testing, explicit counterfactual failures, a refined encoder-ablation interpretation, and an explanation of missing Sachs interventional evaluation. The reorganized presentation also improves accessibility. These are evidence-supported gains, although ambiguous batch documentation and conflicting code-availability descriptions limit the reproducibility improvement.
